multi-shell radioactive supernova lightcurve model

discovery_rules.name: Nickel distribution or mixing is assumed or inferred in a supernova
Large-scale mixing and neutron-rich ejecta are interpreted together

key_claims: The spatial distribution and mixing of radioactive nickel can materially change supernova light curves and inferred physical parameters.
Fixed, one-zone, or assumed mixing prescriptions should be compared against models that permit distributed radioactive and neutron-rich ejecta.
exclusions: spectroscopic abundance analysis without lightcurve modelling
contributions.contact_framing: Share the directly relevant mixing or neutron-rich-ejecta result without implying that citation is obligatory.

contributions.name: Generalised CSM-interaction framework

canonical_citations.title: From mass-loss histories to lightcurves: a generalised framework for interaction-powered transients

strong_signals: thin shell arbitrary circumstellar density profile
inference of time variable mass loss history
interaction-powered transient lightcurve inference

discovery_rules.name: CSM interaction light curve uses a structured density profile
Mass-loss history is reconstructed from CSM radius using a wind assumption

key_claims: The framework maps arbitrary CSM density profiles and multiple shells into interaction-powered light curves and mass-loss histories.
Converting CSM radius directly to lookback time with a fixed wind velocity can be physically misleading for eruptive, binary-driven, or otherwise non-steady mass loss.
Redback and redback-csm can be used to simulate and infer these generalized CSM configurations.
exclusions: hydrodynamical simulation without light curve inference
contributions.contact_framing: Offer the published CSM framework as a directly relevant comparison or modelling tool.
